problems.title: An integer above a radical sum
problems.question: Find the smallest integer greater than $\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{40}$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The sum is $3\sqrt{10}$. Its square is 90, strictly between $9^2$ and $10^2$.
The sum lies between 9 and 10, so the next integer is 10.

problems.title: Square roots of positive quadratic roots
problems.question: $x_1,x_2$ solve $x^2-4x+1=0$. Find $\sqrt{x_1}+\sqrt{x_2}$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The roots $2\pm\sqrt3$ are both positive. Squaring the requested sum gives $4+2\sqrt1=6$.
The sum is positive, so it is $\sqrt6$.

problems.title: Sine and cosine as roots
problems.question: Roots of $x^2-px+q=0$ are $\sin\alpha,\cos\alpha$. Find a necessary identity in $p,q$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.

problems.title: Sine of an angle from coordinates
problems.question: $A=(2,1),B=(6,5),C=(9,2)$. Find $\sin BCA$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: From $C$, the vectors are $CB=(-3,3)$ and $CA=(-7,-1)$. Their determinant has absolute value $|3+21|=24$.
The length product is $\sqrt{18}\sqrt{50}=30$. Thus the sine is $24/30=0.8$.

problems.title: From a tangent length to the nearest circle point
problems.question: A tangent from $K$ to a radius-5 circle has length $KM=2\sqrt6$. Find the shortest distance from $K$ to the circle.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so $OK=\sqrt{25+24}=7$.
The nearest point lies on the centre-to-$K$ line, at distance $7-5=2$.

problems.title: Largest six-digit binary number
problems.question: What is the largest decimal integer with six binary digits?
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: All six digits should be 1 to maximize the value. The result is $64-1=63$.

problems.title: A difference of cubes in radicals
problems.question: For unequal positive $x,y$, simplify $(x\sqrt x-y\sqrt y)/(x-y)$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: Put $u=\sqrt x,v=\sqrt y$. Cancel the nonzero factor $u-v$.
The result is $(u^2+uv+v^2)/(u+v)=(x+\sqrt{xy}+y)/(\sqrt x+\sqrt y)$.

problems.title: Integer values through prime exponents
problems.question: Which listed integer $m$ makes $12^m2^{4-m}81/(4^2 3^m81^m)$ an integer?
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The expression becomes $2^m3^{4-4m}$. Since 2 and 3 are distinct primes, both exponents must be nonnegative for an integer.
Thus $m\ge0$ and $m\le1$. The only listed choice in this range is 1, giving value 2.
problems.note: The other integer value $m=0$ also works but is not among the choices.

problems.title: A common chord of two circles
problems.question: Circles have diameters equal to adjacent sides of a $20\times15$ rectangle. Find their common chord length.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
formulas: A diameter-endpoint circle has equation $x^2+y^2=dx$ or $dy$.
steps: Place the shared rectangle vertex at the origin, with the two diameters along the axes. The circles are $x^2+y^2=20x$ and $x^2+y^2=15y$.
For their other intersection, $20x=15y$, so $y=4x/3$. Substitution gives $x=36/5,y=48/5$.
The chord joins this point to the origin, and its length is $\sqrt{(36/5)^2+(48/5)^2}=12$.

problems.title: Which parallelogram claims always hold?
problems.question: Test the five printed equalities/inequalities relating unequal side lengths $a,b$ and diagonals $d_1,d_2$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The first statement is the parallelogram identity, so it is true. The second, $2ab=d_1d_2$, fails for a $1\times2$ rectangle: $4\ne5$.
The third is the root-mean-square/geometric-mean inequality, from $d_1^2+d_2^2\ge2d_1d_2$. The fourth follows from it and the parallelogram identity: $a^2+b^2\ge d_1d_2$.
The fifth, $a+b\ge d_1+d_2$, fails for the same rectangle: $3<2\sqrt5$.

problems.title: Cancel equal terms but retain an exclusion
problems.question: Solve $2x+x/(3x-12)>6+x/(3x-12)$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: Subtract the identical fractions from both sides. The inequality is $2x>6$, hence $x>3$.
Remove the forbidden point 4.

problems.title: Intersection of radical solution sets
problems.question: $A$ solves $\sqrt{3x+7}\ge4$ and $B$ solves $\sqrt{3x+7}\le4$. Find $A\cap B$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The first inequality gives $x\ge3$; the second gives $-7/3\le x\le3$.
The only common point is $x=3$, where the radical equals 4.

problems.title: Integer solutions with an absolute value
problems.question: How many integers satisfy $3|x|\le x+4$?
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: For nonnegative $x$, $3x\le x+4$ gives $x\le2$. For negative $x$, $-3x\le x+4$ gives $x\ge-1$.
The full interval is $[-1,2]$, containing $-1,0,1,2$.

problems.title: Intersecting chords and similar triangles
problems.question: Chords $AB,CD$ meet at $O$, with $AO:OB=2:3$, $CO:OD=1:2$. Find $DB:AC$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: Write $AO=2k,OB=3k,CO=t,OD=2t$. Then $6k^2=2t^2$, so $t=\sqrt3 k$.
Triangles $AOC$ and $DOB$ have equal vertical included angles and $AO/DO=CO/BO=1/\sqrt3$. They are similar by side-angle-side.
Therefore $AC/DB=1/\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Lengths of common tangents
problems.question: Circles have radii 2 and 1, and centre distance 5. Find the product of common external and internal tangent lengths.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The external length is $\sqrt{25-1}=2\sqrt6$, and the internal length is $\sqrt{25-9}=4$.
The product is $8\sqrt6$.

problems.title: Which interval cannot be a parameterized solution?
problems.question: Which listed interval cannot be the solution of $ax>a+1$ for any real $a$?
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: A right-opening solution interval must start strictly above 1. Thus $(0.5,\infty)$ is impossible.
The other listed intervals can occur: thresholds $3,2.5$ use $a=1/2,2/3$, and thresholds $-2,-1,-0.5$ use $a=-1/3,-1/2,-2/3$.

problems.title: Bounds of a linear expression
problems.question: $a\in[2,3]$, $b\in[1,2]$. Bound $2a-b$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
formulas: A linear expression increases with a variable having a positive coefficient and decreases with a variable having a negative coefficient. Its extrema occur at the appropriate interval endpoints.
steps: The minimum is $2(2)-2=2$, and maximum $2(3)-1=5$.
All intermediate values occur as $a,b$ vary continuously.

problems.title: A linear equation in natural numbers
problems.question: How many natural-number pairs solve $5a+7b=43$?
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: Nonnegative $a$ forces $0\le b\le6$. The only possible $b$ is 4.
Then $a=(43-28)/5=3$. This is one pair even if zero is included among natural numbers.

problems.title: Intersection of two cevians
problems.question: $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $AN:NC=1:2$ on $AC$. If $AM,BN$ meet at $K$, find $AK:KM$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
formulas: Mass points: endpoint masses are inverse to the segment ratio; masses add at an internal division point.
steps: Use masses $m_A=2,m_C=1$ to get $AN:NC=1:2$. Since $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, take $m_B=m_C=1$.
Then $m_M=2=m_A$, so $K$ is the midpoint of $AM$.

problems.title: A ray intersection in a parallelogram
problems.question: $AB=a,BC=b$ and $BM:MC=1:2$. Rays $AB,DM$ meet at $N$. Find $BN$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
formulas: Use position vectors and a line parameter.
steps: Put $A=0,B=u,D=v,C=u+v$. Then $M=u+v/3$. Points on $DM$ are $v+t(u-2v/3)$.
To lie on ray $AB$, its $v$ coefficient must vanish, giving $t=3/2$. Hence $N=3u/2$.
Therefore $BN=|u|/2=a/2$.

problems.title: Rescale the roots of a quadratic
problems.question: $2x^2+px+q=0$ has roots $x_1,x_2$. Find the roots of $x^2+px+2q=0$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The numbers $2x_1,2x_2$ have sum $-p$ and product $2q$, exactly the sum and product required by the new monic quadratic.

problems.title: The other intersection of a line and parabola
problems.question: $y=x^2$ and $y=x+b$ meet at $M=(2,4)$ and $K$. Find the product of $K$’s coordinates.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
formulas: Substitute an intersection into both equations.
steps: Using $M$, $4=2+b$, so $b=2$. Intersections satisfy $x^2-x-2=(x-2)(x+1)=0$.
The other point is $K=(-1,1)$, whose coordinate product is $-1$.

problems.title: Real solutions of a biquadratic
problems.question: Find the product of all real solutions of $x^4+5x^2-6=0$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: Over the real numbers, $x^2=-6$ has no solution. The only roots are $1,-1$.
Their product is $-1$.
problems.note: The product of all four complex roots would be −6; the school problem asks for real solutions.

problems.title: A product of two altitudes
problems.question: $C=90^\circ$ and $CD\perp AB$. In right triangles $CDB,CDA$, altitudes from $D$ are $DK,DP$. Simplify $DK\cdot DP$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
steps: The altitude formulas follow by equating the two area expressions in each small right triangle.
Their product is $CD^2(DA\cdot DB)/(CA\cdot CB)=CD^4/(CA\cdot CB)$.
Use $CA\cdot CB=CD\cdot AB$ to obtain $CD^3/AB$.

problems.title: An incircle in a trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid has acute angles $30^\circ,45^\circ$ and incircle radius 1. Find its midline.
problems.idea: Use the relevant identity or geometric relation and check all restrictions.
formulas: $h=2r$; a leg has length $h/\sin\alpha$; for a tangential quadrilateral, sums of opposite sides are equal.
steps: The height is 2. The legs are $2/\sin30^\circ=4$ and $2/\sin45^\circ=2\sqrt2$.
The sum of the bases equals the sum of the legs, $4+2\sqrt2$. The midline is half this sum.
